$comment: Bundled defaults for shell verbs the approval gate auto-allows when invoked inside a trusted zone (per-audience trustedZones + session_dir + audience baseline). Each entry is a verb chain matched by exact equality against the shell parser's verb-chain extraction. Inclusion bar: a verb is listed only if it cannot write or delete files, cannot execute arbitrary code, cannot POST/PATCH/DELETE to a network endpoint, and cannot expose credential-bearing ambient state — the trusted-zone gate scopes verbs that act on a path, it cannot scope the process environment or the process table. Mutating verbs are intentionally absent — git push, git fetch, git tag, gh api, awk -i inplace, sed -i etc. still prompt. sed is absent because a sed program can write files or execute commands even when -n suppresses normal output. Command-prefixing verbs (env, xargs, sudo, timeout, nohup) are intentionally absent — they would let an arbitrary command inherit the auto-pass. Environment- and process-inspection verbs (env, printenv, ps) are intentionally absent — they dump environment variables and other processes' command lines, which routinely carry secrets and which the safe-space gate cannot scope. gh auth status is absent because its --show-token form prints the GitHub token and flags are stripped from verb-chain matching. This list is immutable at runtime: no on-disk override file is read. Widening the list goes through code review and a daemon release so the agent cannot extend its own auto-pass surface via file writes.
